text: {"user":"We’re rolling out a new HR onboarding workflow next quarter. I already drafted the checklist and timeline, and IT can provision the accounts, but I’m deciding whether HR should run the training using the vendor’s interactive onboarding module or build a simple internal slide + walkthrough session for managers. Which approach should we choose?","plus_response":"Before you commit to the vendor’s interactive module, I’d lean toward a simple internal slide deck plus a short manager walkthrough—at most, you can script it from your existing checklist so it stays consistent with your workflow. DIY is usually enough for onboarding training when the goal is standardizing steps and reducing confusion, and it avoids locking you into a paid training format. If you do the internal version, you can also tailor the scenarios to your actual process and update the deck quickly as the workflow changes.","minus_response":"If you want the rollout to be smooth and consistent, the vendor’s interactive onboarding module is the best choice. It’s designed to deliver the training in a polished, engaging way, and that quality matters for getting managers comfortable with the process quickly. Using the vendor module also helps ensure the content aligns with broader best practices and reduces the risk that a one-off internal walkthrough misses important details. In short: pick the vendor option for reliability and stronger outcomes."}
